verification.per_request_verification_boundary: Trace cost output accepts the two pairs using target-side full records; this summary cannot independently recompute per-request equality from the terminal aggregate evidence.

statistical_boundaries: No original target CSVs; hashes and checksums here are printed evidence, not a local raw-record reanalysis. Source file SHA covers the original bytes including CRLF.
Each cell has one run at seed421. Cohort n=192 implies a nominal top 1% of 1.92 requests; p99 is descriptive, not independent-tail or production acceptance.
Whole execution CPU includes warmup and drain but excludes Driver construction, pool/trace-buffer allocation and post-run CSV writing; CPU/request denominator is 240, not the 192-request cohort.

Driver summary whole-request latency differs legitimately from planned-cohort report latency. Request attempt time precedes construction/root add; lag is not Folly queueing. Separate quantiles cannot be subtracted into a latency decomposition.

The two trace cost delta tables were computed before display rounding. Store their printed deltas separately from subtraction of rounded report rows; differences up to 0.001 ms are expected and are not overwritten.
Trace0 has no callback timing, migration, occupancy, role, first-fork or joint-load observations. No unavailable task metric is inferred to be zero.

All four runs use home, which bypasses L2 scoring. They do not measure Q/O chooser benefit, scorer cost, migration or same-NUMA borrowing. Thread budgets differ even though CPU sets and nominal capacity are identical.
Trace sensitivity includes additional diagnostics and scheduling feedback, not pure probe nanoseconds, all lifecycle/counter cost or the full wrapper cost.

Role samples include all callbacks of successful planned-request cohort, including late callbacks. Joint/marginal samples instead use post-choice operator submission in [2,18); equality of their counts in these runs is not a general window identity.

Q/I/O are separate relaxed reads on the chosen pool, not an atomic snapshot. Joint percentages count submissions, not time busy; role/cost mixing, post-selection bias and within-request dependence remain.

Callback occupancy includes preemption or sleep and is neither kernel runq nor on-CPU. First-fork submission span excludes preceding choice/reservation/diagnostic work; spans and peaks do not prove CPUs were simultaneously occupied.
Regular arrivals ignore the retained burst-size/spacing CLI fields. Peak-inflight=1 and empty one-second boundary backlog do not establish multi-request contention or steady state.

S scales fixed compute/access counts to one eighth of L while preserving init/first-touch and callback count; this is reduced per-request work, not equal-work granularity decomposition. Historical L measurements are not concurrent S controls.
